result.answer:
Based on the site's own rules, **yes — you will need to pay the ¥12,000 assessment fee again for this second claim.**

**The rule:**
> "Claimants with two or more approved claims from separate incidents within any rolling 12-month period are exempt from the ¥12,000 assessment fee. The waiver is applied automatically at lodgement; no separate application is required."
— *Claims FAQ*, [/claims/faq/#fee-waivers](https://office-of-kaiju-affairs.vercel.app/claims/faq/)

This is reinforced by the fee schedule itself:
> "The claim assessment fee is ¥12,000, payable when the claim is lodged."
— *Claim Fee Schedule*, [/claims/fees/](https://office-of-kaiju-affairs.vercel.app/claims/fees/)

**Why it applies to your case:** The waiver threshold is *two or more approved claims* already on record in the trailing 12 months at the time you lodge. You currently have only **one** approved claim (the March incident). Since this new claim — filed three weeks ago's incident — will be your second, not your third, you don't yet meet the "two or more approved" threshold, so the automatic waiver won't trigger at lodgement.

The eligibility engine confirms this: running your situation (zone 4, commercial property, structural damage, 1 prior approved claim in the last 12 months) through the Kaiju Damage Compensation ruleset returns you as **eligible for compensation** (including business-interruption coverage, since Tanaka Bakery is commercial), but it does **not** grant a fee waiver, because that only activates once you have 2+ approved claims already on record — which will only be true starting with your *next* (third) claim within a rolling 12-month window, assuming this second one is approved.

**Bottom line:** Pay the ¥12,000 fee when you lodge this claim. If it's approved, you'll then have two approved claims in the past 12 months, and any further claim within that rolling window would qualify for the automatic repeat-claimant waiver. Separately, note that the fee is refunded in full anyway if your final award exceeds ¥1,000,000 (per the same Fee Schedule page).

normalisations: A field value counts if it CONTAINS the expected value — "Zone 4" satisfies "4".
A boolean counts if it reads as affirmative — "Yes" satisfies true.

A select counts if its visible LABEL matches the expected option value with case and punctuation collapsed — "Structural alteration" satisfies "structural-alteration". A UI agent picks the option it can read; scoring the label as a miss would measure transcription rather than comprehension.

These three were ADDED AFTER defects were found in this scorer, not designed in from the start. Each one existed because a check had already scored an answer wrongly, and the last of them changed a finding that had already been handed over. They are listed so a reader can judge the instrument, including its history.

Answer text is normalised before matching: NFKC, Unicode dashes folded to "-", non-breaking spaces to " ", curly quotes to straight, and markdown emphasis markers removed. A model that writes "rolling 12‑month" or "only **one** approved" is making the same claim as one that does not.
A conclusion is read from position, not vocabulary: a correct answer quotes the rule it applies, so waiver wording inside a quotation does not outrank an explicit finding stated earlier.
Affirmative phrases are only counted when not negated within the preceding ~28 characters, so "should not have to pay" is not read as "have to pay".
